X=(6,2),\quad Y=(3,4),\quad Z=(1,6),\quad T=(5,4).
\]

A rotation can match the endpoints in either order.

1. If \(A\mapsto C\) and \(B\mapsto D\), the centre is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of \(AC\) and \(BD\):
\[
y-2=-2(x-3),\qquad y-4=-\frac13(x-7).
\]
Solving gives \((x,y)=(1,6)\), which is exactly \(Z\).

2. If \(A\mapsto D\) and \(B\mapsto C\), the centre is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of \(AD\) and \(BC\):
\[
7\left(x-\frac92\right)+6(y-4)=0,\qquad -(x-\frac{11}{2})+2(y-2)=0.
\]
Solving gives
\[
(x,y)=\left(6,\frac94\right),
\]
which is not any of the marked points \(X,Y,Z,T\).

Thus among the marked points, only \(Z\) can be the centre.
